data.narrative:
GenFab Co is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Matt Parlmer that has raised $510K to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though peer-set constraints limit direct benchmarking.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($510K) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $1.275M. This method rests on the assumption that the company's prior fundraising reflects its current enterprise value and that stage-to-stage multiple progression holds for this sector and founder quality.

The Peer-Median approach is not applicable. Although ten robotics and manufacturing peers exist in the comp universe (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics), filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies yielded fewer than three datapoints—below the threshold for robust median comparison. Falling back to all-sector medians risks material mispricing given the heterogeneity of robotics subsectors and funding environments.

The triangulated range is $1.08M to $1.47M, centered on $1.28M, supported by a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer anchoring and the degree to which prior fundraising activity meaningfully constrains post-money valuation at the next round.
